concepts.name: Purpose of Maps
concepts.description: Maps are simplified representations of places that help us locate positions, understand surroundings, and plan routes. They provide information that is difficult to visualize from the ground.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the purpose of maps and identify situations where maps are useful.

concepts.name: Map Symbols
concepts.description: Maps use standardized symbols and colours to represent roads, rivers, buildings, parks, railway lines, and other geographical features.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to interpret common symbols and colours used on simple maps.

concepts.name: Map Legend
concepts.description: A map legend or key explains the meaning of symbols used on a map, enabling users to interpret information accurately.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to use a map legend to understand and interpret map features.

concepts.name: Cardinal Directions
concepts.description: The four cardinal directions—North, South, East, and West—help describe locations and movements on a map.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify and use the four cardinal directions to describe locations.

concepts.name: Intermediate Directions
concepts.description: Directions such as North-East, North-West, South-East, and South-West provide more precise location information.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify intermediate directions while reading simple maps.

concepts.name: Planning Routes
concepts.description: Maps help compare different routes and choose the most suitable path based on distance and direction.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to trace and describe routes between two locations using a map.

concepts.name: Locating Places
concepts.description: Students learn to identify the positions of places by observing landmarks, roads, and symbols on a map.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to locate specific places using a simple map.

concepts.name: Drawing Simple Maps
concepts.description: Simple maps of classrooms, homes, schools, and neighbourhoods help students understand spatial relationships and relative positions.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to draw simple maps using appropriate symbols and directions.

concepts.name: Scale Awareness
concepts.description: Although not measured precisely at this level, students understand that maps represent large areas in a reduced size.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain that maps use reduced representations of real places.

concepts.name: Navigation
concepts.description: Maps assist people in travelling, finding addresses, and exploring unfamiliar places using printed or digital maps.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain how maps are used for navigation in everyday life.

concepts.name: Landmarks
concepts.description: Landmarks such as schools, hospitals, parks, and temples help people identify locations and navigate effectively.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify important landmarks on a simple map.

concepts.name: Spatial Reasoning
concepts.description: Reading maps develops the ability to understand positions, distances, directions, and relationships between places.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to use spatial reasoning to interpret and describe map-based information.

concepts.name: Understanding Maps and Navigation
concepts.description: This chapter develops students' ability to read, interpret, and draw simple maps while understanding directions, symbols, landmarks, and navigation.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to read maps, interpret symbols, identify directions, and use maps to locate places and plan routes.
